28:   nothing changes. `(release stock id)` makes a `:quarantined` lot `:active`
29:   again; anything else changes nothing.
30: - `(take-from stock id n now)` returns `[stock' ok?]`. When lot `id` is
31:   usable at `now` and `1 <= n <= :qty`, its `:qty` drops by `n` and `ok?` is

33:   the stock is unchanged and `ok?` is false.

(ns stock.core)

(defn usable?
  "A lot is usable at `now` when it is :active, holds at least 1, and has
  not expired (`now` before `:expires`)."
  [lot now]
  (and (= :active (:status lot))
       (>= (:qty lot) 1)
       (< now (:expires lot))))

(defn receive
  "Add a lot of `qty` of `sku` expiring at `expires`. With `qty` at least 1
  the new lot is :active and gets the next id; returns [stock' id]. With
  `qty` 0 the stock is unchanged and the id is nil."
  [stock sku qty expires]
  (if (>= qty 1)
    (let [id (:next-id stock)
          lot {:id id :sku sku :qty qty :expires expires :status :active}]
      [(-> stock
           (assoc-in [:lots id] lot)
           (update :next-id inc))
       id])
    [stock nil]))

(defn available
  "Total :qty of the usable lots of `sku` at `now`."
  [stock sku now]
  (reduce (fn [acc lot]
            (if (and (= sku (:sku lot)) (usable? lot now))
              (+ acc (:qty lot))
              acc))
          0
          (vals (:lots stock))))

(defn quarantine
  "Make lot `id` :quarantined; with no such lot nothing changes."
  [stock id]
  (if (contains? (:lots stock) id)
    (assoc-in stock [:lots id :status] :quarantined)
    stock))

(defn release
  "Make a :quarantined lot `id` :active again; anything else changes nothing."
  [stock id]
  (if (= :quarantined (get-in stock [:lots id :status]))
    (assoc-in stock [:lots id :status] :active)
    stock))

(defn take-from
  "When lot `id` is usable at `now` and 1 <= n <= its :qty, drop its :qty by
  n (removing it from the stock if it reaches 0) and return [stock' true].
  Otherwise return [stock false]."
  [stock id n now]
  (let [lot (get (:lots stock) id)]
    (if (and lot (usable? lot now) (>= n 1) (<= n (:qty lot)))
      [(if (= n (:qty lot))
         (update stock :lots dissoc id)
         (assoc-in stock [:lots id :qty] (- (:qty lot) n)))
       true]
      [stock false])))

(defn purge
  "Remove every lot that has expired (`:expires` <= `now`), whatever its
  status."
  [stock now]
  (update stock :lots
          (fn [lots]
            (into {} (remove (fn [[_ lot]] (<= (:expires lot) now)) lots)))))

(ns picking.core
  (:require [stock.core :as stock]))

(defn plan
  "The picks that would take `n` of `sku` from `stock` at `now`: a vector of
  [id k] pairs, each taking k >= 1 from lot id. Usable lots are consumed
  first-expiring-first, ties broken by lowest id; each lot is used up before
  the next is touched and the last pick takes only what is still needed.
  With `n` 0 the plan is []; when the usable lots hold less than `n` in all
  the plan is nil."
  [stock sku n now]
  (if (= n 0)
    []
    (let [usable (->> (vals (:lots stock))
                      (filter #(and (= sku (:sku %))
                                    (stock/usable? % now)))
                      (sort-by (juxt :expires :id)))
          total (reduce + 0 (map :qty usable))]
      (if (< total n)
        nil
        (loop [remaining n
               lots (seq usable)
               picks []]
          (if (= remaining 0)
            picks
            (let [lot (first lots)
                  k (min remaining (:qty lot))]
              (recur (- remaining k)
                     (next lots)
                     (conj picks [(:id lot) k])))))))))

(defn pick
  "Fill `order`, a vector of lines {:sku Nat :qty Nat}, in order, from
  `stock` at `now`. Each line is filled by taking its plan's picks through
  `stock.core/take-from`; a line whose plan is nil is short and takes
  nothing, and later lines go on. Returns [stock' report] with

      {:filled [index ...], :short [index ...], :picks [[index id k] ...]}

  :filled and :short hold line indexes in order; :picks holds every pick
  made, in the order made, tagged with its line's index."
  [stock order now]
  (loop [stock stock
         idx 0
         lines (seq order)
         filled []
         short []
         picks []]
    (if (nil? lines)
      [stock {:filled filled :short short :picks picks}]
      (let [line (first lines)
            picks-for-line (plan stock (:sku line) (:qty line) now)]
        (if (nil? picks-for-line)
          (recur stock (inc idx) (next lines) filled (conj short idx) picks)
          (let [[stock' made]
                (reduce (fn [[st made] [id k]]
                          (let [[st' _] (stock/take-from st id k now)]
                            [st' (conj made [idx id k])]))
                        [stock []]
                        picks-for-line)]
            (recur stock'
                   (inc idx)
                   (next lines)
                   (conj filled idx)
                   (into picks made))))))))

input.content:
# Notes on TASK.md

Ambiguities I noticed while implementing, and the reading I chose.

## stock.core

- **`receive` and `qty` values other than 0/at least 1.** TASK.md says
  "When `qty` is at least 1 ... With `qty` 0 ...". Quantities are Nats, so
  negatives cannot occur; I implemented the test as `qty >= 1`, which treats
  any non-positive value the same as 0. Only 0 is actually reachable.

- **`quarantine` / `release` on the "wrong" status.** TASK.md spells these
  out awkwardly: `quarantine` makes lot `id` `:quarantined`; `release` makes
  a `:quarantined` lot `:active` "again; anything else changes nothing". I
  read the "anything else" as applying to `release`: it only acts when the
  lot exists *and* is currently `:quarantined`. So `release` of an already
  `:active` lot, or a missing lot, is a no-op. `quarantine` of a missing lot
  is likewise a no-op (explicitly stated), and re-quarantining an already
  quarantined lot is harmless.

- **`take-from` and removal.** "a lot whose `:qty` reaches 0 is removed from
  the stock." I remove it by dissoc'ing the id from `:lots`; the id is not
  reused (`:next-id` is untouched, so it keeps increasing).

- **`take-from` `ok?`.** I return `[stock false]` with the *identical*
  (unchanged) stock whenever the condition `usable && 1 <= n <= :qty` fails.

- **`purge` expiry test.** "`:expires <= now`" is used literally, and it
  applies regardless of status — so quarantined expired lots go too.

## picking.core

- **`plan` result shape.** A vector of `[id k]` pairs. For `n` 0 it is `[]`,
  even if the sku holds nothing. For `n > 0` with insufficient usable stock
  it is `nil`.

- **Tie-breaks / ordering.** Lots are ordered by `:expires` ascending, then
  by `:id` ascending. I only consider usable lots (`stock.core/usable?`:
  `:active`, `:qty >= 1`, `now < :expires`), so quarantined and expired lots
  are skipped entirely.

- **"each lot is used up before the next is touched".** A pick takes
  `min(remaining, lot-qty)`, so interior lots are fully drained and only the
  final pick is partial. A lot with `:qty` 0 is never a pick (it is not
  usable).

- **`pick` and plans recomputed per line.** Each line's plan is computed
  against the stock *as it stands after the previous lines*, so a later line
  sees quantities already consumed. A `nil` plan means the line is short and
  nothing is taken from it (never partly filled); later lines still run
  against the unchanged stock.

- **Returning the picks.** `:picks` entries are `[line-index id k]`, appended
  in the order the picks are made. `take-from`'s `ok?` is not surfaced; a
  plan is guaranteed valid when executed immediately, so it is always true.

- **Line indexes.** Indexes are positions in `order` (0-based). A qty-0 line
  is `:filled` with no picks. `:filled` and `:short` preserve line order; an
  empty order yields `{:filled [] :short [] :picks []}`.

- **Empty order / missing keys.** Not specified beyond the above; I assume
  `order` is a vector of well-formed `{:sku ... :qty ...}` lines and `stock`
  always has `:lots` and `:next-id`.

part.text:
Done.

**Implementation** (`src/stock/core.clj`, `src/picking/core.clj`), committed as `b5a6252 implementation`:
- `receive` adds an `:active` lot under `:next-id` when `qty >= 1`, returning `[stock' id]`; `qty` 0 returns `[stock nil]`.
- `available` sums usable lots of the sku; `quarantine`/`release` mutate only where specified; `take-from` enforces `usable && 1 <= n <= qty`, drops qty, and removes the lot at 0; `purge` drops everything with `:expires <= now` regardless of status.
- `plan` filters to usable lots, sorts by `:expires` then `:id`, drains each before the next, partial only on the last pick, `[]` for n=0 and `nil` when short.
- `pick` recomputes each line's plan against the evolving stock, executes picks through `stock.core/take-from`, and reports `{:filled ... :short ... :picks [[line id k] ...]}` in order.

**Verified** with `jolt -e`: ordering/ties (`[[1 3] [2 4] [0 3]]`), short lines taking nothing while later lines proceed, qty-0 lines filled with no picks, quarantine/expiry refusals, and nil/empty plan edges.

**NOTES.md** written, covering the ambiguities I found: the `>= 1` vs `= 0` reading of `receive`, the "anything else changes nothing" scope for `release`/`quarantine`, lot removal without reusing ids, literal `:expires <= now` purge, per-line plan recomputation, and the 0-based line-index/pick ordering.

NOTES.md is left untracked, since the commit instruction covered the implementation. Say the word if you'd like it committed too.
